unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 2: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 — Calculate interim-compensation and appeal-deposit amounts using the correct statutory base and conditional wording

facts.statement: Statutory section 143A permits the court to order interim compensation with a ceiling of 20 percent of the cheque amount at its stated procedural stages. Section 148 permits an appeal deposit with a floor of 20 percent of the trial-court fine or compensation, additional to interim compensation. Text gives 60 days with a court-directed extension up to 30 days on sufficient cause and repayment with specified interest on acquittal. Application and case law require separate verification.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 150–151, 164–165; PDF page = printed page + 19

payload.title: A shared percentage can conceal a different legal base
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Section 143A** concerns interim compensation during trial. In the statutory text, the court may order it at the specified stage, and the amount must not exceed **20% of the cheque amount**. This is a ceiling on the amount of such an order.

**Section 148** concerns a deposit on appeal against conviction. Its stated minimum is **20% of the fine or compensation awarded by the trial court**, and the deposit is additional to interim compensation. This is a floor with a different base.

The text also supplies payment periods, possible court-directed extensions for sufficient cause and repayment provisions after acquittal. These are conditional court processes. Do not describe the two percentages as automatic deductions made by a bank, or infer a mandatory order in every case. Current judicial interpretation and exam-cutoff applicability remain under review.

self_check.prompt_text: Which quantity is the base for each percentage?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Section 143A uses the cheque amount; Section 148 uses the trial-court fine or compensation.

payload.title: Compare the two percentage bases before calculating
payload.core_explanation_md:
A training file has a cheque amount of **Rs 7,50,000** and a trial-court compensation award of **Rs 9,00,000**. For the arithmetic illustration, assume a Section 143A order at its 20% ceiling and a Section 148 order at its 20% floor.

The first base is the cheque amount: 20% gives **Rs 1,50,000**. The second base is the trial-court award: 20% gives **Rs 1,80,000**. If both stated amounts are payable, the appeal deposit is additional, giving **Rs 3,30,000** in this illustration.

Do not swap the two bases, assume every court makes an order, or present the floor and ceiling as a single fixed tariff. This example teaches arithmetic under the stated statutory-text assumptions; judicial application remains subject to review.

self_check.prompt_text: Why are the two 20% amounts different?
self_check.expected_takeaway: They use different bases: cheque amount for Section 143A and trial-court fine or compensation for Section 148.

worked_steps.description: Interim-compensation ceiling on the cheque amount.
Appeal-deposit floor on the trial-court award.
Add the two assumed orders; the appeal deposit is additional.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Interim ceiling Rs 150000; appeal floor Rs 180000; combined assumed orders Rs 330000.

payload.stem_md: A training worksheet uses the cheque amount to calculate both the Section 143A ceiling and the Section 148 floor, although the trial-court award differs. Which correction is required?

options.text_md: Use the cheque amount for 143A and the trial-court fine or compensation for 148
options.explanation_md: The statutory percentages have different bases; equal percentages do not justify using the same amount.

options.text_md: Use the account balance as the base for both
options.explanation_md: Neither stated percentage is based on the drawer's current account balance.

options.text_md: Treat both percentages as compulsory bank service charges
options.explanation_md: They concern conditional court orders, not bank charges automatically debited on dishonour.

options.text_md: Subtract interim compensation from the appeal base before applying the floor
options.explanation_md: Section 148 describes the deposit as additional to interim compensation; the worksheet cannot invent this base reduction.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The statutory percentages have different bases; equal percentages do not justify using the same amount.

payload.stem_md: For this statutory-text arithmetic exercise, a court makes a Section 143A order at the stated 20% ceiling on a cheque for Rs 465000. What is that ceiling in rupees? This does not assume that an order is automatic in every case.

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give a whole number of rupees without commas. All figures are exact; no rounding is needed.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The stated ceiling uses the cheque amount: 465000 × 20 / 100 = 93000 rupees.

worked_solution_steps.description: Apply the stated proportion to the correct statutory base.

payload.stem_md: For this statutory-text arithmetic exercise, the trial court awards compensation of Rs 680000. An appeal order under Section 148 directs a deposit at the stated 20% minimum. Interim compensation of Rs 70000 has already been paid. What is the additional appeal deposit in rupees?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give a whole number of rupees without commas. All figures are exact; no rounding is needed.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The appeal floor uses the trial-court award: 680000 × 20 / 100 = 136000 rupees. The earlier 70000 rupees is not deducted from that base; the deposit is additional.

worked_solution_steps.description: Apply the stated proportion to the correct statutory base.
